packet.prompt: Read only the supplied images. No web, search, repository context, catalogue, or other readings. Do not infer an identity from familiarity. These are manuscript fragments on bindings; distinguish host text and labels from the fragment. First report orientation, staves, clefs, and surviving musical runs. For each usable run give the image and approximate location, then note positions as integers in diatonic staff steps relative to the first note (0), preserving adjacent repeats. Prefer 6-14 or more consecutive notes where legible; describe uncertainty and stop at a gap or hidden span. Say which marks might be custos rather than sung notes. Report visible clef shape and line if secure; do not guess absolute pitch. Give a short literal reading of any accompanying words, with uncertainty, without completing from memory. If possible record two separate passages for later comparison. If no reliable continuous run of at least four notes remains after repeated pitches collapse, explain the visible limitation. A difficult image is not automatically unreadable: inspect the actual crops. Do not write readings of an image you could not view. Finish with coverage and limitations. Save the entire response as response.txt in this packet directory. Do not modify prompt, images, or packet.json.

text:
IMAGE-ONLY FIRST READING

Orientation and surviving notation

All eight supplied images were successfully viewed, including the six detail images. Image-001 is an upright overview of a binding with the manuscript strip running horizontally across its middle. The Gothic manuscript text reads left to right in the displayed orientation; the blue printed binding label and round labels are rotated relative to it. Image-002 is the other binding surface, substantially covered by pasted paper and adhesive remains. Images-003/004 enlarge the left/right portions of the upper surviving music row; images-005/006 enlarge the left/right portions of the lower row. Images-007/008 enlarge the obscured surface shown in image-002.

The readable face has red staff ruling and brown, broad square/lozenge notation. Two musical rows survive, with some text above and between them. In the lower row, three clear red lines are visible, plus an upper line at or very close to the fold; this appears to be a four-line staff. The upper row has the same arrangement but its upper part is especially affected by the fold. At the left of both rows is a vertically split, two-lobed angular mark, consistent with a C-shaped clef. Its opening appears to embrace the uppermost staff line at the fold. I would record “C-like, apparently top line” provisionally, not assign absolute pitches: the upper lobe is partly cut/folded and the shape is not completely preserved.

Conventions below: 0 is the first note of each separately reported run; +1 is one diatonic staff position higher, -1 one lower. Adjacent repetitions are retained. The integer readings come from position relative to the local ruling, not from an assumed tune or absolute pitch. Locations refer to approximate image pixels.

Run A: lower row, right detail, image-006

The clearest useful continuous run begins at the square head near x=200, y=175 and continues through the broad head near x=1300, y=420. Reading:

0, -1, -2, -3, -2, -1, -1, -2, -4

The individual anchors are approximately:
x=200: second visible line from the top, y=175;
x=310: space below it, y=230;
x=420: next line, y=295;
x=510: next space, y=350;
x=630: line, y=295;
x=710: space above that line, y=235;
x=920: same space, y=230;
x=1000: line, y=300;
x=1300: bottom line, y=425.

The x=310/420/510 figures are descending lozenges; the x=630/710 figures rise. The repeated -1 at x=710 and x=920 is intentional. The middle figure around x=920/1000 descends one staff step. This nine-note run remains eight events after adjacent equal pitches collapse, so it comfortably exceeds the requested minimum. The page is slightly skewed, and the heads are broad, but the line-versus-space placement in this passage is substantially clearer than in Run B.

A further square-looking mark near x=1570, y=305 would add -2, giving:
0, -1, -2, -3, -2, -1, -1, -2, -4, -2.
I do not include it unconditionally as a sung note. It is isolated toward the end of the surviving row and could be a custos, though its fairly ordinary square head does not establish that. There is no text below this row in the surviving strip to settle the issue. At the far left edge of image-006 there are cropped heads belonging to the preceding material; I start at x=200 rather than invent their missing context.

Run B: lower row, left detail, image-005

This is a separate passage from Run A, although both belong to the same staff and the image details overlap. Starting at x=400, y=190 and proceeding to the head near x=1490, y=305, my provisional positional reading is:

0, 0, 0, -1, +1?, -1, -1, -2

Approximate anchors:
x=400 and x=695: two separate squares on the line near y=190;
x=900 to x=1040: an oblique connected figure, apparently from that line down to the following space, hence 0, -1;
x=1100: a higher square-like head, apparently in the space just above the y=185 line, hence +1?, with its lower edge touching/crossing the line;
x=1160: following lower head in the space near y=245, hence -1;
x=1430: another head in the same space, hence -1;
x=1490: head on the line near y=305, hence -2.

This is less secure than Run A. In particular, the oblique shape around x=900–1040 needs two-note interpretation, and the head at x=1100 is unusually tall and close to the line: 0 instead of +1 is a live alternative. Thus the uncertainty is not merely a choice of absolute pitch. I would preserve these uncertainties for comparison rather than treat this as an exact independent fingerprint.

There is then a square at x=1700 on the same lower line (-2), followed by a vertically arranged lower and higher pair near x=1780. Their positions appear to be -1 and +1 respectively, but the order within the connected figure is less directly shown than the single heads. A tentative extension is therefore:
0, 0, 0, -1, +1?, -1, -1, -2, -2, {-1, +1 in probable ascending order}.
I would use the shorter eight-event version first, with its stated uncertainty. The rightmost compound is also visible at the cropped left edge of image-006; it must not be counted twice when combining the photographs.

Upper row: images-003 and -004

In image-003, the two clear heads left of the blue label are near x=350, y=575 and x=610, y=690. They give 0, -2. The label then hides a long span, so this cannot be joined directly to the visible material on its right.

Image-004 contains a long but largely repeated-pitch stretch. The partial head at its left edge lies about one staff step above the following squares. Provisional reading from that clipped leftmost head through the square near x=1810:
0, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1.
The pitch repetition is clearer than any syllabic grouping, and some portions of the head boundaries are crossed by fold/label damage. After repetition collapse it supplies only two events and is not a distinctive four-event run. The angular/triangular mark at the extreme right, near x=1870 and the fold, might be a custos rather than another sung note. I exclude it. The round labels obscure text and lower parts of the row, so no inference across their covered areas is warranted.

Literal text and labels

The manuscript text is faint and should not be completed from a familiar phrase. In image-003 the upper text permits approximately “…udens” (uncertain preceding letter and internal strokes), followed farther right by “ma…” or “na…”. Beneath the staff, left of the blue label, I can make out approximately “…ic et…”, with the initial sequence uncertain. Image-004's upper line has an ending resembling “…tione” and a following sequence beginning “doce…”; subsequent letters are not secure enough for a full word. Its lower text is too incomplete and overlain by labels for a reliable connected reading. These are tentative visible letter groups, not proposed chant text or an identification. No accompanying words survive below the usable lower-row runs in images-005/006.

The blue label visibly includes printed “… FRANCO…” and “1699”; the white round label reads “N” and “1602”. Another round label bears crossed-out handwriting/numerals. These are later binding/catalogue labels, not manuscript lyric text; their numbers provide no musical pitch or textual evidence. I make no identification from them.

Obscured face and coverage limits

Images-002, -007, and -008 show extensive paper/adhesive coverage, horizontal dark rules, regular dotted vertical marks, and faint show-through. I cannot separate a continuous sequence of noteheads with usable staff positions there; I do not transcribe music or words from that surface. The dotted grid-like marks are not treated as notation.

Coverage: viewed images-001 through -008, re-inspected image-005 for its compound figures, reported the usable lower-right run, a qualified lower-left passage, and the disconnected/repetitious upper-row remains. The principal secure melodic evidence is Run A's nine-event contour. Run B requires review of the oblique figure and the tall head before exact matching. Fold losses, opaque labels, cropped edges, and the possible final custos prohibit constructing a complete melody or absolute-pitch transcription. No external source, catalogue, remembered identity, or other reader's result was used.
